sections.title: Phase 1: High-Leverage Utility Functions (@lifeos/utils)
sections.content:
**dates.ts** → JSDoc for getWeekStart(), formatDate(), and any re-exports from date-fns
- Add: Usage examples showing timezone handling, week boundary behavior
- Inline: Comment any non-obvious logic around DST or month boundaries

**macros.ts** → Document TDEE calculation, macro cycling, P/C/F split logic
- Add: JSDoc with examples showing input ranges, why cycling matters for bulking/cutting
- Inline: Explain why certain divisors are used, edge cases for minimal calorie days

**cost.ts** → Document budget calculations, projection logic, category rollups
- Add: Parameter descriptions, return type specs, example inputs/outputs
- Inline: Why certain costs are attributed to weeks vs. months

**scheduling.ts** → Document block placement, conflict detection, timezone conversions
- Add: Examples of typical schedules, edge cases (daylight saving, cross-timezone)
- Inline: Logic for muscle group spacing (48-hour buffer), why certain patterns fail

**Other utilities** (logger.ts, errors.ts, performance.ts, readiness.ts, nutritionFeedback.ts, rrule.ts): Follow same pattern—JSDoc + examples + non-obvious logic comments

---

sections.title: Phase 2: Lambda API Route Documentation
sections.content:
**Each Lambda module** (ai-scheduler, workouts, nutrition, planner, grocery, health, supplements, auth, finances):
- List all routes (method + path) in module README
- Add JSDoc to each route handler function explaining: what it does, who calls it (web/mobile/cron), what it validates (Zod schema), what errors it throws
- Document input/output shape with examples

**Example route documentation**:
```
POST /v1/workouts → createWorkout(event)
Validates: WorkoutCreateSchema (Zod)
Returns: { success: true, data: Workout }
Throws: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 409 (spacing conflict)
```

---

sections.title: Phase 3: Complex Logic Documentation
sections.content:
**Pipeline V2 (runPipeline.ts)**: Document 7-stage execution (foundation → week_shape → workouts/meals/supplements → aggregate → verify), parallel fanout, error recovery
- Inline: Why stages run sequentially, what happens on timeout, how results propagate

**Rate Limiting**: Document daily caps per scope (full: 5, partial: 4, sickDay: 10)
- Inline: Why certain triggers increment counters, how reset works

**Muscle Spacing**: Document 48-hour buffer logic, why it matters (CNS recovery)
- Inline: Edge cases (week boundaries, timezone midnight), why specific muscle groups can coexist

**Macro Cycling**: Document bulk/cut/recomp phases, weekly adjustments
- Inline: Why certain formulas prevent metabolic adaptation

---

sections.title: Phase 4: Module READMEs
sections.content:
Create for each package and Lambda module:
- **Purpose**: One sentence explaining what it does
- **Key Exports**: List of exported functions/types
- **Usage Examples**: Typical call patterns
- **Integration Points**: How it connects to other modules
- **Error Handling**: Common error codes and what to do

---

sections.title: Execution Order (by impact):
sections.content:
1. @lifeos/utils/macros.ts, cost.ts, scheduling.ts (used by 20+ routes)
2. ai-scheduler Lambda routes (core scheduling trigger)
3. Pipeline V2 orchestration (system brain)
4. Remaining utilities (dates, logger, errors)
5. Other Lambda modules (workouts, nutrition, planner, etc.)

This approach prioritizes functions with highest call-site density—improving their documentation multiplies impact across the codebase.
</summary>

<analysis>
The LifeOS codebase requires systematic documentation across three layers: (1) Lambda API handlers (10 modules with ~120 routes), (2) Utility packages in @lifeos/utils (dates, macros, scheduling, cost, logging, errors), and (3) Complex orchestration logic (Pipeline V2, rate limiting, muscle spacing, grocery aggregation).

From the examined context:

**Handler Pattern** (from .claude/rules/lambda.md): All Lambda handlers follow a standard structure with router-based dispatch. The ai-scheduler-lambda/handler.ts exemplifies this—it's already well-documented with dual entry points (EventBridge cron + API Gateway). The pattern is: OPTIONS preflight → route matching → handler invocation → error handling with structured logging.

**Key Undocumented Areas**:
- pipelineRoutes.ts: The main API surface for Pipeline V2 (POST /generate-pipeline, GET /pipelines/:id, POST /stages/:stage/retry) lacks inline documentation despite being the critical flow orchestrator.
- @lifeos/utils modules: dates.ts, cost.ts, scheduling.ts, macros.ts have minimal JSDoc. These are heavily used across 10 Lambda modules and web components—they're high-leverage targets.
- Complex logic: Pipeline V2 runPipeline.ts (7-stage sequential + parallel fanout), rate limiting (daily caps per scope), muscle group spacing (48-hour buffer logic), macro calculations (TDEE, cycling, P/C/F splits), grocery aggregation (deduplication + quantity rollup), cost projections.

**Documentation Leverage**: Focusing on @lifeos/utils first yields maximum impact—each exported function serves 3-5 Lambda routes + 10+ web components. Pipeline orchestration comes second because it's the system's heartbeat.

**Constraints from existing patterns**:
- JSDoc format: @param {type} name, @returns {type}, @throws {type} error
- Comments explain WHY not WHAT (per CLAUDE.md preferences)
- Inline comments only for non-obvious logic (hidden constraints, workarounds, subtle invariants)
- Examples show typed usage, not pseudo-code
- E
